title: n8n Tutorial for Beginners 2026 (Your First Workflow)
summary: n8n tutorial shows how to wire nodes together to automate web requests. Turn incoming webhooks into spreadsheet rows and Slack messages without code.
body_markdown:
## Run the same workflow in Activepieces if n8n's limits get in the way


### Rebuilding the job for better pricing


If the scale and pricing questions are your constraint, you can rebuild the same webhook, Google Sheets and Slack job in Activepieces. It's an open-source automation tool with an MIT-licensed core, a free cloud plan that needs no card, and self-hosting.


It doesn't import n8n workflows. You rebuild each one by hand, so **the cost of switching is your build time** , and it's smallest while you have one workflow.


### How the two tools compare


Below, two sentences set the tools side by side on the points that decide the first ten minutes. The takeaway is that the license and the sign-up terms differ, while the work of moving is the same either way.


n8n uses the Sustainable Use License, offers a time-limited trial that needs no card, and can be self-hosted under that license, with nodes maintained by n8n.


Activepieces has an MIT core, a free cloud plan with no card, self-hosting, and integrations listed at activepieces.com/integrations; in both directions, workflows are rebuilt, not imported.


If you self-host or embed the tool in something you sell, the license difference matters most. MIT and the Sustainable Use License set different limits on what you may do. Read the license text before you commit, not after.


### Rebuild steps and checking the result


To count as done, the workflow must behave as it did on n8n, with the same trigger, the same row appended, and the same message sent.


1. Create a flow and choose the[Webhook](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/webhook) integration as the trigger. Copy the URL it gives you and send a test request so the payload shape is captured.
2. Add the[Google Sheets](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/google-sheets) integration, connect your account, and map the payload fields to the columns of the sheet.
3. Add the[Slack](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/slack) integration, connect the workspace, and build the message from the same mapped fields.
4. Publish the flow, repoint whatever calls the old webhook at the new URL, and keep the n8n version running until a real event has passed through both.


Step 4 is the one people skip. Running both until one live event succeeds gives you a rollback path.


### When staying on n8n is the right call


Stay if your workflow already runs and you have no limit pressing on it. A rebuild buys nothing there.


Stay too if you depend on a node that has no matching integration; check the integrations directory for each app before you start.


If you do want to test the move,[sign up for Activepieces](https://cloud.activepieces.com/sign-up?ap_cta=blog_body&ref=%2Fblog%2Fn8n-tutorial-for-beginners-2026-your-first-workflow) and rebuild the three steps above; flows are unlimited on every plan, including free, so the test costs you build time and nothing else.


Where a flow runs should never decide whether you can leave, and here it doesn't: cloud and self-hosted share one codebase, and Git Sync and Releases, a documented feature, carries a flow from the free plan to your own Docker, Compose or Kubernetes install, with RBAC, SSO, SCIM and audit logs on both.


MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.
